subject: cs201
question: Explain why a hash table lookup is O(1) on average but O(n) in the worst case.
student_answer:
Average case is O(1) because a good hash function spreads keys evenly so each bucket
has very few entries. Worst case is O(n) because if many keys hash to the same bucket, 
you end up having to scan through all of them one by one, which is linear.
student_feedback: Great job! Your answer clearly explains both the average-case efficient distribution and the worst-case collision scenario.
instructor_feedback: The student successfully covers both criteria. For c1, they explicitly state that a good hash function spreads keys evenly so buckets have few entries leading to O(1). For c2, they correctly identify that many keys hashing to the same bucket causes a linear scan of all entries, resulting in O(n).

same total afterward — nothing just vanishes or appears out of nowhere. That's because
a reaction doesn't destroy or make new atoms, it just shuffles the existing ones around
into different combinations.
student_feedback: Great job! You clearly explained both what the law of conservation of mass is and why it holds true at the atomic level.
instructor_feedback: The student successfully met both criteria. For c1, they correctly stated that mass is neither created nor destroyed (phrased as mass starting with is the same as the end without vanishing or appearing). For c2, they explicitly explained that atoms are shuffled/rearranged rather than created or destroyed.

question: Explain the concept of opportunity cost.
student_answer:

several options and chose one, opportunity cost is the benefit of whichever other

subject: physics101
question: State Newton's second law and use it to find the acceleration of a 4 kg object when a net force of 20 N acts on it.
student_answer: Newton's first law says an object keeps its state of motion unless a force acts on it, and the third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The second law, which is the one that matters here, says the net force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration, F = ma. Rearranging gives a = F / m, so with F = 20 N and m = 4 kg the acceleration is 20 / 4 = 5 m/s², in the direction of the net force. This is also why a heavier object accelerates less under the same force.
student_feedback: Great job! You stated Newton's second law correctly and accurately calculated the acceleration with the right value and units.
instructor_feedback: The student correctly stated Newton's second law (F = ma) fulfilling criterion c1. They also correctly calculated the acceleration as 5 m/s² and included the proper units, fulfilling criterion c2.
